Archive provenance

Recovered. Reorganized. Reconnected.

A record of what survived, where it came from, and how it shaped the new website.

Selected snapshots

  • May 16, 2014 homepage: earliest available homepage in the calendar; clear welcome, roster, frequency list and original navigation.
  • June 29, 2014 gallery: names, call signs and 19 recoverable member thumbnails.
  • December 26, 2018 homepage: fuller navigation, operator recruitment, updated roster and Mount Ord photograph; page marked updated September 12, 2018.
  • September 3, 2018 operator script: roll call, visitors, second round and closing; page marked updated June 5, 2016.

The September 16, 2026 homepage capture redirected to an unrelated travel domain and was excluded. Selection reflects the useful versions inspected, not a claim that every capture was exhaustively audited.

Recovered assets

24 image files: 19 member thumbnails, two gathering thumbnails, two banner GIFs and the Mount Ord photograph. Original binaries and a source manifest are included with the project. Six attempted gallery assets were unavailable or returned invalid image responses.

What changed

  • Table-based navigation became semantic, responsive pages with keyboard navigation and visible focus states.
  • Joining instructions, operator information, community guidance and archive material have separate destinations.
  • Outdated repeater settings and rosters are explicitly historical; current repeater guidance links to ARA.
  • The historic gallery has readable captions and alternative text.
  • Obsolete chat, stream embeds, old contact addresses and repeater-control codes are not active features.
  • The rebuilt site runs without third-party scripts, external fonts or a database.

What still needs confirmation

Current contact information, a supported streaming or chat service, and a public address for 2100NetLog. No contact form pretends to send messages, and no sample members or live net status have been invented.

Logging integration

The local 2100NetLog project already provides public net pages and protected operator tools. This site is an independent community front end. A future link to its public pages can connect visitors to live and past net sessions without exposing private station records.
